blocks.text: `up` reconciles the running state with the file; `down` removes containers and networks (volumes only with -v); `exec` enters an existing container while `run` creates a new one-off.

rows: Keeps named volumes; `-v` deletes them (data loss)
New container from the service definition; starts deps; no ports unless `--service-ports`
Merged, interpolated config: the debugging tool

blocks.text:
$ docker compose up -d --build --wait
$ docker compose exec -T db pg_dump -U app -Fc rag > rag.dump
$ docker compose run --rm api python -m app.scripts.reindex
$ docker compose down -v      # wipes data

Q: "You edited compose.yaml and ran docker compose restart, but nothing changed. Why?" A: "restart reuses the existing containers and their old config. docker compose up -d compares the desired state and recreates changed services."

items: exec vs run: existing vs new container.
